Robot Doctor Drivetrain

Robot moves on its own

Creeps or drives when nobody is touching the controls. Below are the 3 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 4 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Does it start moving when you press INIT, before PLAY? Select the OpMode, press INIT, and watch the robot.
  • Does the robot move as soon as you press PLAY, before anyone touches the gamepad? Press PLAY with hands off the gamepad.
  • If you unplug the gamepad and plug it back in with the sticks untouched, does it stop? Stop the OpMode first, then replug, then reassign with START + A.
  • With hands off, does telemetry show stick values that aren't 0? Print gamepad1.left_stick_x, left_stick_y, right_stick_x in telemetry and leave the gamepad alone.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Gamepad zeroed with a stick pushed

The Driver Station sets stick center when the gamepad connects. If a stick was bumped then, the robot thinks you are always pushing.

How to fix it 1 min

  1. Stop the OpMode, unplug the gamepad, and plug it back in with both sticks untouched.
  2. If a gamepad dropped mid-match while a stick was pushed, wiggle the sticks and let them return to center before restarting.
  3. Re-assign the gamepad: START + A for driver 1, START + B for driver 2.

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues

2 Worn sticks with no deadzone

Older gamepads rest slightly off center, so the robot creeps when nobody touches it.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Print the raw stick values in telemetry while not touching anything. Anything above about 0.05 is drift.
  2. Add a small deadzone in code, or swap to a newer gamepad.
Simple deadzone
double deadzone(double v) {
    return Math.abs(v) < 0.08 ? 0 : v;
}

double y = deadzone(-gamepad1.left_stick_y);

Sources: FTC Docs · Gamepad best practices

3 Missing waitForStart()

In a LinearOpMode, code before waitForStart() runs on INIT, so the robot can move before you press PLAY.

How to fix it 2 min

  1. Make sure every LinearOpMode calls waitForStart() before any movement code.
  2. Only do setup (hardwareMap, directions, resets) before it.
Correct structure
@Override
public void runOpMode() {
    // setup only
    leftDrive = hardwareMap.get(DcMotor.class, "leftDrive");

    waitForStart();

    while (opModeIsActive()) {
        // driving code goes here
    }
}

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues
